method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 16's east margin prints 'AVE. F. OR CHURCH' with the adjoining-sheet numeral '61'; sheet 61's west margin prints 'AVE. F. OR CHURCH' with the adjoining numeral '16', so the two sheets meet inside Ave F. The 31st St hundred-block changes across it: sheet 16 draws the 500 block (502 504 506 ... 522 524 north side, 501 503 505 ... 521 523 south side) between Ave E and Ave F, while sheet 61 draws the 600 block (602 604 606 ... 622 624 / 601 603 605 ... 621 623) between Ave F and Ave G. Sheet 16's own west corridor is labelled 'AVE. E. OR POST OFFICE' and sheet 61's east corridor 'AVE. G. OR WINNIE', bracketing Ave F. Avenue frontage runs 3002-3028 and 3102-3128 (30th-31st, 31st-32nd) appear on the Ave F face of both sheets. Positions: sheet 16 draws only Ave F's west block face (native x 3068) plus ~13 ft of pavement to its neatline (3116/3128); sheet 61 draws its neatline (106/114) and the east block face (native x 251). Centres placed 30 ft inside each face using each sheet's own scale (80 ft numbered-street width = 242 native px on 16, 256 px on 61); the two neatlines then land ~13 ft west of centre on both sheets, confirming the fit. The detection candidates (2777 on 16 = G.H.&N. R.R. switch/block interior of block 451; 398 on 61 = block interior) were both rejected.
